method.grid: 40x24 over the 160x96 luma, 4x4 px per cell
method.the_semantic_channel: the cell's LOCAL GEOMETRY -- activity, log-change and edge gradient -- and NOT its brightness
method.the_alphabet: fitted per room by k-means over that descriptor, with the characters assigned by the clusters' mean activity so the mapping is a function of the room's own data
method.the_cardinality: chosen by the SILHOUETTE of the training descriptors -- a truth-blind rule.  The first version chose k by the agreement with the truth, which is a selection on the metric; the whole per-k curve is recorded so the effect is measured
method.the_refusal: a synthetic-device session is computed and then refused, so the refusal is a decision

the_ties.the_reading: the truth is a NEAR-TIE in most sessions (the luma's per-half change energy has a median ratio of 1.17 and a minimum of 1.00), so the question is hard by construction and the raw agreement is not measuring much unless the ties are separated out.  Both numbers are reported.

summary.the_holdout: the alphabet is fitted on the first half of the frames and the even columns; the question is answered over the odd columns, and graded against the FULL-RESOLUTION luma so the agreement is not a tautology
summary.the_cardinality_rule: k is chosen by the silhouette of the training descriptors, which never looks at the truth.  Had k been chosen by the agreement with the truth -- the first version's rule -- the number below would have been the optimistic bound instead

the_optimistic_bound.the_reading: the two rules disagree about the cardinality on some sessions, and where they disagree the truth-chosen k is the optimistic one by construction -- which is why it is the bound and not the headline

the_negative_glyph_iou.what: the grid's observed mask against the PIXEL-LEVEL coverage -- the majority of a cell's pixels changed above the noise floor.  The grid pools the change first and this pools the votes, so the IoU is what the 4x4 pooling costs
